prompt:
Investigate this repository without changing any tracked files or adding non-ignored files. Trace the reservation request through the actual code, not just the CLI example. Return ONLY one JSON object with the following keys; do not use Markdown fences.
Use one fresh harbor.models.State and call harbor.app.handle sequentially, always POST /v1/reservations. Start with harbor.examples.HEADERS and BODY (copy them before changing):
1. accepted: the complete response for the unchanged example.
2. replay: the complete response when sending the same example again.
3. closed: response for project="old" AND amount="not-money" (all other fields unchanged).
4. denied: response with authorization="Bearer wrong" and the unchanged body.
5. over_budget: response for amount="12.35" and request_id="req-18", otherwise unchanged.
6. summary: the complete harbor.reports.summary after those five requests.
7. stages: list the module-qualified function names on the successful path from handle through the journal commit in invocation order. Include handle, routes.resolve, auth.authenticate, service.reserve, every direct helper invoked by reserve, journal.commit, responses.created, and audit.record; omit nested standard-library calls and any functions not invoked on this path. All names must start with harbor.
8. replay_skips: list the three module-qualified functions called directly by reserve after its idempotency lookup on a new request but skipped on replay, in invocation order.
Explain precedence using the exact status/code/origin values in the response objects. No prose is necessary. The JSON is the deliverable; leave the repository unchanged.
